source.name: Wikidata (CC0)
source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?released WHERE { { SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(COALESCE(STR(?pubT), ""), "|", COALESCE(STR(?pubP), "")); separator=";") AS ?pub) (GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(COALESCE(STR(?incT), ""), "|", COALESCE(STR(?incP), "")); separator=";") AS ?inc) WHERE { { SELECT ?item ?sitelinks WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q9143 ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . FILTER(?sitelinks > 25) } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 200 } OPTIONAL { ?item p:P577 ?pubSt . ?pubSt a wikibase:BestRank ; psv:P577 [ wikibase:timeValue ?pubT ; wikibase:timePrecision ?pubP ] . } OPTIONAL { ?item p:P571 ?incSt . ?incSt a wikibase:BestRank ; psv:P571 [ wikibase:timeValue ?incT ; wikibase:timePrecision ?incP ] . } } GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . BIND(IF(CONTAINS(?pub, "-"), ?pub, ?inc) AS ?released) OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 199

first_released.sort: from the oldest to the newest
first_released.shot: In what year was the programming language {label} first released?

rows.label: C
rows.hook: underlies most operating systems and shaped the syntax of countless later languages

rows.label: JavaScript
rows.hook: runs inside every web browser and brings web pages to life with interactivity

rows.label: C++
rows.hook: added object-oriented features on top of an older language and powers demanding software like game engines

rows.label: R
rows.hook: is favored by statisticians and data scientists for analyzing data and making charts

rows.label: Java
rows.hook: runs the same compiled code on any device thanks to a write once, run anywhere design

rows.label: Go
rows.description: programming language developed by Google and the open-source community
rows.hook: was designed to make writing large-scale backend software simple and fast

rows.label: assembly language
rows.description: any low-level programming language in which there is a very strong correspondence between the instructions in the language and the architecture's machine code instructions
rows.hook: gives programmers instructions that map almost one-to-one onto a processor's own machine code

rows.label: SQL
rows.description: relational database language that allows to extract from data tables a series of records with selection, sorting and computation criteria, or to update, delete or add records
rows.hook: lets people ask relational databases to fetch, sort, and update stored records

rows.label: TypeScript
rows.description: programming language, superset of JavaScript that compiles to JavaScript
rows.hook: adds type safety on top of the web's dynamic scripting language, catching bugs before code runs

rows.label: COBOL
rows.hook: still powers many banks' and governments' old mainframe systems handling daily transactions

rows.label: Fortran
rows.hook: was built for scientists and engineers doing heavy numerical calculations and still runs in supercomputers

rows.label: Perl
rows.description: interpreted programming language first released in 1987
rows.hook: earned a reputation as the duct tape of the early web for quickly processing text and scripts

rows.label: F#
rows.hook: blends functional and object-oriented programming styles for building reliable software

rows.label: Lua
rows.hook: gets embedded inside games and apps as a small, fast scripting layer for custom behavior

rows.label: Haskell
rows.hook: forces programmers to write in a purely functional style with no hidden side effects

rows.label: MATLAB
rows.hook: is the go-to tool engineers use for matrix math, simulations, and plotting technical data

rows.label: Swift
rows.hook: was built to make writing apps for phones and computers safer and more modern than older tools

rows.label: Ada
rows.hook: was designed for safety-critical systems like aircraft and rockets where a single bug can be fatal

rows.label: PL/I
rows.hook: tried to combine business, scientific, and systems programming into a single all-purpose language
